digest.component_or_area: LLM capability routing and provider profile resolution
propositions: output_mode() and runner.py cache logic currently make decisions by string-matching provider names (anthropic prefix, hardcoded provider set), causing Bedrock-hosted Claude to silently lose caching and fallback to prompted structured output despite native capability

pydantic-ai exposes per-vendor capability records at model.profile (ModelProfile) with fields like supports_json_schema_output and bedrock_supports_prompt_caching that correctly reflect capabilities across direct APIs and Bedrock hosting

ModelProfile cannot be read via isinstance(BedrockModelProfile) in CI because BedrockModelProfile is exported only from pydantic_ai.models.bedrock which imports botocore; instead capability detection must use field presence (bedrock_supports_prompt_caching attribute) and safe isinstance checks (AnthropicModelProfile from SDK-free pydantic_ai.profiles.anthropic)

a new leaf module capabilities.py must implement capabilities_for(model_or_string) returning ModelCapabilities with native_structured_output, prompt_cache_style, and supports_thinking fields, plus a _PROFILE_RESOLVERS registry for lazy-string resolution and an override table applying Claude-specific rules across both AnthropicModelProfile and BedrockModelProfile

lazy model strings created by S1 for unsupported providers (openai, google) must have their profiles resolved without importing those SDKs, via pydantic_ai.profiles.* which are pure capability records and import cleanly without vendor SDKs

rebar override table must predicate on profile type and capability fields (not provider name strings) and enforce that Claude (both direct Anthropic and Bedrock-hosted) gets native_structured_output=False to preserve PromptedOutput reliability, while groq explicitly transitions from NativeOutput to PromptedOutput since groq_model_profile reports supports_json_schema_output=False
